name: issue_821_comfort_floor_fallback_no_confidence
description: Issue #821 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). Reproduces the reported live incident (Zone 'Simulated 2'): a warm day with no nat-vent session and NO thermal model, indoor decays below comfort_heat (70F) and the thermostat sat in cool confirming a cooling setpoint every cycle for 2+ hours. Under Design D thermal-model confidence is not an input at all: the first evaluation with indoor below the floor (08:30, 67F vs 70F, from a 73F cooling-zone baseline) arms heat, and later cycles (08:35, 08:41) simply re-affirm it. File name kept for traceability.
source: Issue #821 investigation — live incident, Zone "Simulated 2" (climate.simulated_thermostat), indoor held at 57F for 2+ hours while CA repeatedly confirmed a 74F cool setpoint every cycle with zero corrective heating.
notes: Occupant impact: a zone with no thermal-model history (new zone, or too few HVAC cycles) must still have its comfort floor defended. The house must get heat on the first evaluation below 70F instead of sitting at 57F with the AC armed.

Design D rule exercised (docs/08 section 6f): indoor < floor -> heating immediately; thermal confidence, day type, recency and sustain are not inputs. The 08:35 and 08:41 evaluations are redundant re-affirmations of the already-armed family (they model the ~5-minute cadence of the live incident) and are kept because they prove heating stays armed across repeated cycles instead of being reset or re-escalated. See issue_827_off_day_floor_breach_escalates.json and issue_827_missing_forecast_fallback_escalates.json for near-duplicates of this event shape.

Baseline fix (Issue #1066 review): the original baseline sat inside the heat zone (indoor <= floor + m), so heat was already armed before the breach and the final-state assertions passed vacuously. The baseline is now inside the cooling zone so the breach reading is the first thing that can arm heat. (Band [70F, 74F] is only 4F wide, so the arming margin is clamped to one third of it, 1.33F: heat zone <= 71.33F, cool zone >= 72.67F. The old 71F baseline armed heat at 08:00.)

Classification fields: day_type=warm with hvac_mode=off, as classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_WARM (the original hand-set hvac_mode=cool diverged from the classifier and was corrected during the #1066 review).

Harness limit: comfort_family reads the engine's FINAL state, so it is placed on the last event; it cannot prove WHEN heating was armed. The tighter timing evidence for this rule is in issue_1066_cold_morning_mild_day_arms_heat_immediately.json (comfort_family_switch_by at the first evaluation).

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main), a warm day is natively cooling and heat is against-grain: the first below-floor evaluation only arms a candidate, escalation needs a 90 s sustain across two evaluations and the 600 s dwell clock, and the dwell clock (see Issue #823) must not be reset by reassertions. A regression that re-introduced a cooling default with no thermal model would leave comfort_family=cooling and fail the final assertion.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('thermal confidence is not an input'; 'indoor < floor -> heating').

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: a newly added zone drifts arbitrarily cold with the thermostat confirming a cooling setpoint every cycle and zero corrective heating, as in the live incident.

events.note: Warm-day classification (classifier derives hvac_mode=off). No nat-vent (fan_mode disabled).
Baseline: indoor 73F in the cooling zone of the narrow band [70F, 74F] (margin 1.33F, cool zone >= 72.67F): cool is armed at 74. No breach.
Indoor has decayed to 67F, below comfort_heat=70F. No thermal model was ever set on this engine (confidence none), which is irrelevant to the selector.
First evaluation with indoor below the floor: floor breach, heat is armed immediately (no sustain, no recency window, no confidence gate).

Realistically spaced re-evaluation (5 minutes later, matching the live incident cadence). Indoor is still below the floor; heating is already armed, so this is a re-affirmation, not a second escalation.
Final re-evaluation: still below the floor, heating remains armed and heat is commanded at comfort_heat.

assertions.reason: Baseline: warm day, indoor within band — comfort band arms normally (proves the scenario's own baseline setup is sound before the below-floor decay).

By the final evaluation the engine is in the heating family. Placed on the last event because comfort_family reads the engine's final state. Heating was actually armed at the first below-floor evaluation (08:30); this checkpoint confirms it holds across repeated re-evaluations. This is the fix for the reported live incident (confidence_k_passive == 'none' throughout).

verdict.summary: On a warm day with no thermal-model confidence, indoor below the comfort floor arms heat on the first evaluation and stays armed.
verdict.observed_behavior: Family is cooling/ceiling at 71F; the 08:30 reading of 67F (below the 70F floor) arms heating and commands heat; later cycles re-affirm it.
verdict.expected_behavior: The comfort floor is never left undefended because the thermal model has no confidence yet: below the floor means heat, immediately (docs/08 section 6f).
